paper_metadata.title: THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF 1.0-2.5 mm THICK SHEETS OF AK4-2ch HIGH-TEMPERATURE STRENGTH ALLOY

evidence.quote: AK4-1ch alloy of the A1-Cu-Mg-Fe-Ni system possesses a satisfactory combination of the above properties, which makes it the most commonly used high-temperature strength aluminum alloy.

evidence.quote: The melting was done in a 300 kg electrical furnace.
The 160 x 540 mm flat ingots were cast in a sliding mold with filtration of the molten metal through a glass screen.
To produce clad sheets the 140 mm thick milled homogenized slabs were rolled with 5 mm thick cladding layers of ADO alloy

parameters.deformation: four passes transverse to h = 80 mm, then eight passes longitudinal to h = 6 mm

evidence.quote: were rolled with 5 mm thick cladding layers of ADO alloy at 400°C in the transverse direction in four passes to a thickness of h = 80 mm and then in the longitudinal direction in eight passes to h = 6 mm
After process annealing at 420°C the 800 mm wide sheets were rolled to room temperature to h = 2.5, 1.5, and 1.0 mm.

attributes.size: about 35 µm average cross section of dendritic cells
attributes.morphology: network of eutectic precipitates bordering the dendritic cells

evidence.quote: In the microstructure of the homogenized ingot there is a network of eutectic precipitates of insoluble A19FeNi phase bordering the dendritic cells with an average cross section of about 35/zm (Fig. 2).
This may be explained by the presence in AK4-2ch alloy of dispersed inclusions of AI3Zr phase retarding grain growth.
